Read MongoDB Dates in an API Response as UTC Date-times

Source: R/wildobs_dp_download.R
dot-api_date_fields.Rd

The WildObs API sends date-times as MongoDB extended JSON, {"$date": "2022-12-20T20:32:18Z"}. jsonlite converts these itself, but when a field in one response mixes dates with nulls (an optional field such as classificationTimestamp) it reads the dates in the computer's local time zone instead of UTC, shifting every one of them by the local UTC offset. So the dates are unwrapped to plain text before parsing, and converted here instead. .api_date_fields() lists the fields sent as dates, .unwrap_api_dates() turns each date object into its text, and .api_dates_to_utc() converts those fields of the parsed records to POSIXct in UTC.

Usage

.api_date_fields(txt)

.unwrap_api_dates(txt)

.api_dates_to_utc(records, date_fields)

Arguments

txt

Character. The raw JSON text of an API response.

records

The records parsed from the unwrapped text, usually a data frame.

date_fields

Character. The fields sent as dates, from .api_date_fields().

Value

.api_date_fields(): the field names. .unwrap_api_dates(): the JSON text with each date object replaced by its date text. .api_dates_to_utc(): the records, with each top-level date field as POSIXct in UTC. A field holding text that is not a UTC date is left as text, for apply_schema_types() to handle.
